A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the nanowire substrate thermal transfer is the major heat dissipation route in current-carryng GaN nanowire devices, whereas the nanoscale thermal conductivity in the nanowire is relatively low, which is likely due to phonon confinement and interface scattering effects.

the heat dissipation in current-carryng GaN nanowire devices can be effectively probed and quantified by combining SThM and spatially resolved micro-Raman spectroscopy, and the heat is mainly dissipated through the nanowire substrate interface.

the nanowire substrate interface thermal resistance is the main contributor to the total heat dissipation, whereas the nanoscale contact interface thermal resistance is a secondary contributor to the total thermal resistance in current-carryng GaN nanowire devices.
